pack.title: Flaky friends
pack.description: Address repeated cancellations without a character attack.

scenarios.setting: A friend cancels at the last minute for the third time.
scenarios.jab: Sorry, something came up again. Rain check?
scenarios.goal: Address repeated cancellations without a character attack.

replies.line: Let's plan again when you can commit to a time.
replies.why: It changes the planning pattern without judging the reason for this cancellation.
replies.delivery: Pause, then say “Let's plan again when you can commit to” at a steady, conversational volume.

replies.line: Choose a time you can keep.
replies.why: It places the next proposal with the person who canceled.
replies.delivery: Say “Choose a time you can keep” clearly, then stop instead of adding a defense.

replies.line: I miss seeing you; last-minute changes are hard, so please suggest a time that feels realistic.
replies.why: It communicates both care and the impact of repeated cancellations.
replies.delivery: Keep “last-minute changes” descriptive, with no emphasis on “again” as an accusation.

replies.line: Our rain checks are starting a weather archive.
replies.why: A shared joke names the pattern without calling your friend unreliable.
replies.delivery: Keep “Our rain checks are starting a weather archive” light; let the joke stand without repeating it.

followUp.line: I'm explaining how the cancellations affect me; I still want a plan we can keep.
followUp.why: It returns to the practical issue rather than defending your personality.
followUp.delivery: Pause before “I'm explaining how the cancellations affect me,” keep the volume even, then allow an answer without reopening your decision.
